intro.text: Jennings reads the whole Bible through one causal chain. A lie about God is believed; that breaks the circle of love and trust; broken trust breeds fear and selfishness; and from that condition flow sin, suffering and death. Once the lie is in place, everything else gets misread too: God's law looks like imposed rules, wrath and fire look like inflicted punishment, and the cross looks like appeasement. The remedy runs the chain backwards: truth restores trust, love is poured in, the heart is healed, and the believer grows up through the levels of moral maturity. Follow the eight nodes in order, or jump to the one that is troubling you.

chain_quote.text: This is what happened in Eden. Satan told lies about God. Adam and Eve believed those lies and the circle of love and trust was broken. Broken love and trust result in fear and selfishness (also known as survival-of-the-fittest). Fear and selfishness result in acts of sin (destructive behaviors). Acts of sin result in damage to mind, character and body – a terminal condition.
chain_quote.speaker: Jennings

title.text: A lie about God is believed

gloss.text: Everything starts with the serpent's five words in Eden: "you will not surely die." Jennings traces every downstream distortion back to one believed lie about God's character and about what sin does.

quotes.text: God created everything in the universe to operate on love, unmitigated giving, beneficence and regard for others more than oneself. God created all beings to be in unity and harmony. But this unity, harmony and love was broken. How? A lie was told. A lie was believed and pain, suffering and death followed.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: Inspiration is clear, God is love and the source of life. Sin breaks the circle of love and separates us from the source of life. Because of this we die. When we accept the “lie” and say God must kill, not only do we make God out to be the source of death, but we support Satan’s original lie that sin does not result in death.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: “You most certainly will not decay and die!” the serpent said to the woman.

title.text: The circle of love and trust breaks

gloss.text: Believing the lie does something inside us: trust in God collapses and distrust takes its place. Jennings calls this the broken "circle of love and trust", and everything after it is downstream damage.

quotes.text: Imagine you are married and someone tells you a lie that your spouse is having an affair. If you believe the lie, will something in you change? Will the circle of love and trust get broken? Will the broken love and trust lead to a change in behavior?
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: When Adam believed the lies about God and broke the circle of love and trust, his rule of love changed to one of fear and selfishness—and nature followed. The drive to survive—kill or be killed, Satan's antagonistic principle of me-first—infected the entire world.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Adam answered, “I heard you in the garden and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid.”

title.text: Fear and selfishness take the heart

gloss.text: Without trust, the mind defaults to self-protection: fear drives selfishness, which Jennings equates with the survival-of-the-fittest instinct. This is the condition the Bible calls sin, and it is terminal if not healed.

quotes.text: The more fearful we become, the more self-focused we become. Fear impairs relational growth!
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: Fear and selfishness in the world today is commonly known as survival-of-the-fittest. The me-first, survival of the fittest mindset is destructive and leads only to death.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: In love, there is no fear. Fear is part of the infection of selfishness, but is purged by love, as fear has to do with concern for oneself. The one who remains self-focused and afraid has not been healed by God’s love.

title.text: God's law misread as imposed rules

gloss.text: Once God is distrusted, His law gets read like human law: made-up rules enforced by threatened punishment. Jennings insists God's laws are design laws, the protocols life is built to run on, where breaking them causes the damage directly.

quotes.text: God as Creator built space, time, matter, energy, and life. His laws are the constants — the protocols, the principles — upon which the universe and life is constructed to operate.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: Human beings did not and cannot create reality as God did; instead, when we make up rules, we must enforce those rules externally, most often through the infliction of punishment. Sadly, after Constantine “converted,” the idea that God’s law functions in the same way that human laws do was embraced; the idea that God’s law is imposed (imperial) began to infect Christianity — corrupting the saving truths that Jesus brought.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: Then, when the selfish desire is accepted by the will, it results in choices that deviate from God's design for life; and choices that deviate from God's design for life result in death.

gloss.text: Under imposed law, wrath becomes God hurting people, fire becomes torture and judgment becomes a verdict. In design law, wrath is God reluctantly letting go, fire is the life-giving glory of His own presence, and judgment is an accurate diagnosis of what is.

quotes.text: This letting go by God, this setting free to reap the consequences of our own persistent, rebellious choices, is what the Bible calls “God’s wrath.” Paul tells us the “wrath” of God occurs because of persistently rejecting God, refusing the knowledge of Him, and preferring our own way over God’s.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: God’s judgment is not a legal finding but an accurate diagnosis of what is. His judgment does not determine who is saved or lost but confirms who chose to be saved or lost.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: for our "God is a consuming fire"–a consuming fire of love, holiness, purity, righteousness, goodness, and truth.

gloss.text: If the problem is an angry God, the cross becomes a legal payment to calm Him down. Jennings' healing substitution reads it the other way: Christ took our terminal condition into Himself to cure humanity, not to pay a penalty.

quotes.text: Similarly, we also believe the Penal Substitution Model (PSM) is laden with pagan ideology from the Dark Ages. The PSM shifts the sin problem away from the sinner’s terminal condition, which is in need of healing, to an offended and angry God who needs appeasing.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: Christ is our substitute. He became human and took sinful mankind’s position. He took our terminal condition upon Himself. He “became sin who knew no sin,” in order to cure mankind from sinfulness.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: He took upon himself our sinfulness (our terminal condition) and in his own person carried it upon the cross so that we could be freed from sin and live the right way — loving God and others more than ourselves. You have been healed by the Remedy procured by his painful ordeal.

gloss.text: The chain runs in reverse. The truth about God seen in Jesus removes the lie, trust returns, and in trust the heart opens so God can pour His love in (Romans 5:5). The result is a new heart with the law of love written back into it.

quotes.text: When we trust in God, we open the heart and the Holy Spirit takes the victory of Christ and reproduces it in us. We get a new heart and right spirit, are reborn, have the law written into the heart/mind, … This is salvation, healing, renewal, regeneration, which only comes by faith in Jesus.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: When we come to know God, as revealed in Jesus, the lies are removed and trust is restored. In this state, God pours His love into our hearts (Romans 5:5) and this love removes our concern for self thus casting out fear of what happens to us.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: And our hope will not be disappointed, because God pours out his love into our hearts and thereby matures, ennobles, and restores us into his image by the Holy Spirit, whom he has given to us.

gloss.text: Healing is also maturing. Jennings describes seven levels of moral decision-making; the same act can be done at any level, but for a different reason. The key shift is from level four (rules and imposed punishment) to level five (love for others), where the law finally lives in the heart.

quotes.text: There are seven levels of understanding right and wrong (moral decision-making). Because God is love, God speaks to each person at their level of development, just as a parent speaks to their children in different ways at various stages of development. A parent explains things differently to a 3 year old than to a 30 year old. So does God.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

quotes.text: Finally, those operating at level four and below are not trustworthy, because they require some external threat to do what is right. Only level five and above can be trusted, because those levels are where the law is written on the heart, when we actually love God and others, understand and value His methods and willingly participate in His purposes.
quotes.speaker: Jennings

scripture.remedy: But the solid food of truth is for the mature, who, by constant use, have trained their faculties to distinguish true from false, good from evil, healthy from unhealthy.

baylor.text: …the predominant view of God is that he is authoritarian, dictator-like. Less than one in four see him as a God of love.
baylor.speaker: Jennings

ocr_note.text: The OCR line reads 'survey of views of God in 4 America' (stray footnote digit) and ends 'love.-' (footnote mark). Quote starts after the digit; the trailing hyphen artefact is not included.

finding.text: In researching what separated those who participated in the killing from those who helped protect the refugees, researchers discovered it came down to one factor: those with authoritarian God concepts participated in the killing, while those with loving God concepts protected the refugees—regardless of denomination.
finding.speaker: Jennings

context.text: Over one million people were killed in four months, and the primary killing zones were churches!
context.speaker: Jennings

what_mattered.text: What mattered was whether they saw God as love—the One who is the designer, or whether they worshiped a dictator—one who makes up rules and enforces them by imposed punishments!
what_mattered.speaker: Jennings

love_unites.text: It is love and love only that unites, that overcomes rules, that transcends arbitrary laws, and that supersedes doctrinal differences. It is love that heals the heart!
love_unites.speaker: Jennings
love_unites.also_at: line 728 (repeated as a KEY POINTS FROM CHAPTER 5 bullet, ending with a full stop)

intro.text: Keith Johnson is an online friend who has worked for years in prison ministry teaching inmates about God's design law, helping them to move past imposedlaw constructs of right, wrong, and justice. He developed four questions to help them understand more clearly what justice is from God's viewpoint.
intro.speaker: Jennings

prompt.text: Take a moment and answer each of the following questions for yourself:
prompt.speaker: Jennings

questions.text: 1. What if I told you that your youngest child was murdered? Would you want mercy or justice for the perpetrator?
questions.speaker: Keith Johnson (quoted by Jennings)

questions.text: 2. What if I told you that the murderer was your oldest child? Would you want mercy or justice for the perpetrator?
questions.speaker: Keith Johnson (quoted by Jennings)

questions.text: 3. What if I told you that you are guilty of the murder of the only begotten Son of God? Would you want mercy or justice as the perpetrator?
questions.speaker: Keith Johnson (quoted by Jennings)

questions.text: 4. What if I told you that you had a daughter, your only daughter, the apple of your eye, who has never given you a moment's grief. Tonight you happen to have a tux hanging in the closet because tomorrow, as her father, you are scheduled to walk your daughter down the aisle and give her away to someone of whom you approve. If you're the mother, you have a new dress hanging next to her wedding gown, a wedding you have been planning and preparing for since the first time you held her in your arms. But tonight, your daughter is at a bachelorette party with her peers, and they talk her into having "one for the road," the first ever in her life. Two, three, four, five, six, seven (drinks) later, while on her way home, she wipes out a school bus full of little children on their way to camp. Everybody aboard the bus dies in a fiery inferno, but your daughter survives. Do you want mercy or justice for your daughter? And ... what do those who are related to the victims who were on the bus want?
questions.speaker: Keith Johnson (quoted by Jennings)

commentary.text: Human justice is based on human law, imposed rules, is motivated by selfishness, and seeks vengeance in the name of justice. The selfish heart has an ingrained sense of justice that in reality is nothing more than vengeance, which is easily exposed because such justice is sought only so long as it doesn't apply to them or theirs.
commentary.speaker: Jennings

gods_justice.text: ustice in God's universe is entirely different. God's justice always seeks to deliver,heal,restore, setright, fix, and save everyone who will allow God to dp o. It is the justice of love—the law of God on which God's government runs
gods_justice.speaker: Jennings

newtown.text: Consider the justice those grieving parents of the children murdered in Newtown, Connecticut, on December 14, 2012, would choose, if they had the choice: punishment for the perpetrator or resurrection and restoration of their children and restoration of a Christlike heart into the perpetrator?
newtown.speaker: Jennings

newtown_continuation.speaker: Jennings

key_points.text: The human imposed-law construct infects all of Christianity regardless of denomination.
key_points.speaker: Jennings

key_points.text: Biblical justice is delivering the oppressed, not punishing the oppressor.
key_points.speaker: Jennings

key_points.text: Legal adjustment of one's account doesn't matter, what matters is love—transforming love that reshapes the heart, that casts out fear, that overwrites selfishness, that overcomes survival instincts, and that bridges the gulf between heaven and earth and connects us again to our Father of love.
key_points.speaker: Jennings

key_points.text: Christ is longing to return for his bride—the church. But he isn't coming backfor a child bride.
key_points.speaker: Jennings

key_points.text: God is not the enemy we must fear—God is our Creator who longs to heal us from the terminal sin-condition that is killing us.
key_points.speaker: Jennings

intro.text: Following are just a few doctrinal statements demonstrating that the infection of imposed law, with its false idea that God is the problem that needs fixing, can be found across the landscape of Christianity—regardless of denomination:
intro.speaker: Jennings

intro_context.text: Further, this evidence is not intended to represent the off- Cial position of any one denomination, person, or group but to demonstrate that the infection of imposed law is common, deeply rooted, and accepted within Christianity as a whole.
intro_context.speaker: Jennings

intro_context_note.text: 'off- Cial' is an OCR artefact for 'official'.

quote.text: God is personally offended by sin and thus he needs to be personally appeased in order to offer a personal forgiveness.
quote.speaker: Roman Catholic theology (Robert Sungenis, Not By Faith Alone; quoted by Jennings)

quote.text: We affrm that the atonement of Christ by which, in his obedience, he offered a perfect sacrifice, propitiating the Father by paying for our sins and satisfying divine justice on our behalf according to God's eternal plan, is an essential element of the Gospel.
quote.speaker: Evangelical theology (D. Neff, 'A Call to Evangelical Unity', Christianity Today; quoted by Jennings)

ocr_note.text: 'affrm' is an OCR artefact for 'affirm'; the trailing 'g' endnote mark is not included.

quote.text: The wrath of God was satisfied.... All other understandings of the cross in the Bible are themselves dependent on penal substitution.
quote.speaker: Southern Baptist theology (Albert Mohler, 'The Wrath of God Was Satisfied'; quoted by Jennings)

quote.text: For a loving God to maintain His justice and righteousness, the atoning death of Jesus Christ became "a moral and legal necessity." God's justice requires that sin be carried to judgment. God must therefore execute judgment on sin and thus on the sinner.
quote.speaker: Seventh-day Adventist theology (Seventh-day Adventists Believe, 1988; quoted by Jennings)

quote.text: Instead of turning his angry face upon us, God turned his angry face upon his son. God's eyes flashed fire, his nose compressed like a spring under pressure and, with locked jaw and clenched teeth he poured out upon Jesus the wrath we deserve.
quote.speaker: Baptist pastor David King, 'God Isn't Looking at Us with an Angry Face' (quoted by Jennings)

context.text: An article by a Baptist pastor recently appeared in my local paper revealing this infection in layman's terms. The article was titled "God Isn't Looking at Us with an Angry Face."
context.speaker: Jennings

meta.title: Come and Reason Knowledge Centre
meta.subtitle: Interactive studies of Dr Timothy R. Jennings' teaching, built from the blog, The Remedy, the tracts and the two God-Shaped books. Start with a sixty-second diagnostic, follow the chain, or search everything.

intro.text: Five pages so far. Each is a single file that opens from disk, remembers your answers in this browser, and shares one imposed-law / design-law switch with the others.

built.title: The Seven Levels of Moral Development
built.pitch: Why does a child brush their teeth? The toothbrush ladder, an eight-question quiz, the seven levels one by one, and why one level cannot easily see another.

built.title: Two Lenses: the Biblical Keyword Switcher
built.pitch: Twelve Bible words (justice, wrath, judgment, forgiveness, atonement…) re-defined under imposed law and under design law, with an entry quiz, flip-card doctrines and Newton's test of what a law is.

built.title: The Falling Dominoes and the Healing Cascade
built.pitch: One lie about God knocks over trust, then love, then motive, then behaviour, then the body. Watch the four dominoes fall and stand again, run the marriage thought experiment, and sort twelve case files.

built.title: The Consuming Fire
built.pitch: Who can dwell with everlasting burning? Sixteen sections on the fire that is God's own presence: the combustion test, the fire gallery, forty-nine verses under two lenses, wrath as letting go, the two deaths, the lake of fire timeline and an objections desk.

built.title: Same Act, Seven Reasons
built.pitch: Seven people brush their teeth, seven condemn a wife-beater, seven say Jesus died for them: the act is the same, the reason is not. Pick an act and a level and hear it re-voiced; see the seven theories of why Jesus had to die.

built.title: Sin Is a Disease: symptom or condition?
built.pitch: A frightened fifteen-year-old asks what sin is, and a psychiatrist answers with cystic fibrosis: bad acts are symptoms, the fearful selfish heart is the condition. Sort symptoms from the disease, choose what the dying patient needs, then turn the Atonement Prism and read every metaphor of the cross under imposed law and design law.

built.title: Wrath = Letting Go
built.pitch: "He gave them over." God's wrath as the withdrawal of protection and Satan's wrath as power used to harm: two animated hands, Romans 1 hotspots, what God said against what happened, the four winds and seven bowls, Egypt's plagues against the last plagues, the cross, a verse wall of every "let go" in The Remedy, and an acting-or-withdrawing quiz.

built.title: The Four Judgments
built.pitch: Eden to the Great White Throne as four non-judicial events: our judgment of God (Carmel, Romans 3:4, the first angel), God's therapeutic diagnosis of each heart (the investigative judgment re-read, Malachi 3, Hebrews 8:10, Daniel 7 as a royal court), the saints' review of history during the thousand years, and the final unveiling where the books are medical records and the gates stand open. A scrubbable timeline that asks "who is judging whom?" at every station, a courtroom/clinic lens switch, a sort lab, ledger-or-medical-record flip cards, a Daniel 7 panel, and an objections desk.

imposed.title: You read through the imposed-law lens
imposed.text: Most of your first readings heard a ruler who makes rules and enforces them by inflicted punishment. That is the default most of Christianity inherited, so it is a good place to begin: the Two Lenses page shows twelve Bible words switching meaning when the lens changes.

mixed.title: You switch lenses without noticing
mixed.text: Some of your readings heard a ruler, some a physician. The Falling Dominoes page shows why the two readings cannot both be true, because they describe different causal chains: one where God inflicts, one where sin destroys and God heals.

design.title: You read through the design-law lens
design.text: Your first readings heard a Designer whose laws describe how life works and whose judgment diagnoses rather than sentences. The Consuming Fire page is where that lens is tested hardest: every fire text in Scripture, read both ways.
